The `build-release.yml` file is a github workflow that automatically creates a pull request that publishes your development changes when merged.

# Workflow setup
To use this workflow properly, you must first have a `"main"` and a `"dev"` branch exist on your repository.

And second, configure your github repo settings at `https://github.com/username/repo-name/settings/actions` to enable:
- ✔ Allow all actions and reusable workflows 
- ✔ Workflow Read and write permissions
- ✔ Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests

# Workflow usage

You should never be pushing directly into `main`.<br>
You should nearly always be pushing to the `dev` branch when working on the modpack, or often when collaborating with others another branch like `deepa/bombRangefix` that you will later merge into `dev`, not `main`.<br>

Once you are done working on your files and are ready to create a release, edit `minecraft/CHANGELOG.md` adding a new changelog entry.<br>
E.g. the 1.0.0 here:

```
# Changelog

## [1.1.0]
### Changes
Fixed that one bad thingy
Added florpus

## [1.0.0]
### Changes
Intital Release
```

After editing this file and pushing it to the `dev` branch, the workflow will automatically create a pull request that you can merge into `main`.

Upon merging said automatically generated pull request, it will run the release actions to publish<br>
a github release, alongside a curseforge release if you have properly supplied your repository<br>
the necessary tokens from your curseforge project and account (See below for Curseforge releases).

Note that the workflow replaces contents of several files
- Replaces DEV with your releases version number in `pakku.json`, `modpack_version_meta.json`, `config/fancymenu/customization/title_screen_layout.txt` (For if you have fancymenu and a custom title with a version number)
- Replaces the Minecraft & modloader versions in serverpack files
- Removes entries with `"export": false` in pakku.json from `config/crash_assistant/modlist.json` to avoid crash assistant logs telling users that they removed mods like ProbeJS or Worldedit, which are meant for dev environment only.

## Github Releases:
When merging the generated pull request a github release will be created automatically with the version tag.

The release contains:
- The regular importable modpack file, and a serverpack file.
- Your own changelog messages that you added to `CHANGELOG.md`.
- An autogenerated changelog from the commits that were put into the release.
- A "Full changelog" which shows the file differences in all the commits compared to the last release.
- All of the first-time contributors with commits in the release.

# Curseforge release action setup:
In your github repo you must set your variables for the Curseforge release actions to function.

Example Link for location to set your variables (Replace with your username and repo name):<br>
`https://github.com/username/repo-name/settings/secrets/actions`

## Repository secrets:<br>
See link for setting a repository secret: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets#creating-encrypted-secrets-for-a-repository<br>
See link for generating a curseforge API token: https://authors-old.curseforge.com/account/api-tokens<br>

Sign in with curseforge, type out the name of your new token in the textbox, then hit `"Generate Token"`.<br>
I just name my token `"splendid_ranching_actions"` or whatever my modpack name is.

In the tab named Secrets you should be on when opening the "`Secrets & Variables`" tab:<br>
**CURSEFORGE_TOKEN** = `f485696b-dd2b-4ede-ad8f-b465cb418695` (Example token value)

## Repository variables:<br>
In the tab named variables you need to click on named "Variables"<br>
**CURSEFORGE_ID** = `1385814` (The numeric ID on your modpacks curseforge page)
